docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Peekniko helps you inspect network requests and responses in your app.

docs.title: Configure Peekniko
docs.text:
Configure Peekniko once when your app starts, before creating your HTTP client:

import peekniko.Peekniko

Peekniko.configure {
    // Add any storage options here, or leave empty to use the defaults.
}

By default, Peekniko keeps captures in memory. To keep them between app launches, add SQLDelight storage.

docs.title: Open Peekniko
docs.text:
import peekniko.Peekniko

Peekniko.open(context)

Peekniko also posts a quiet notification listing the latest calls; tapping it opens the inspector. It asks for the notification permission the first time its screen opens, unless your app has already asked.

docs.title: Ktor
docs.text: Connect Peekniko to your Ktor client by installing its plugin.

docs.title: Gradle dependencies
Install the Ktor plugin
docs.text:
import peekniko.ktor.plugin
import io.ktor.client.HttpClient

val client = HttpClient {
    install(Peekniko.plugin)
}

With this setup, Peekniko captures requests and responses in debug builds and skips them in release builds.

Add the interceptor
docs.text:
import peekniko.okhttp.interceptor

val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
    .addInterceptor(Peekniko.interceptor)
    .build()

With this setup, Peekniko captures requests and responses in debug builds and skips them in release builds.

docs.title: SQLDelight storage
docs.text: Keep your captured requests and responses between app launches with SQLDelight storage.

docs.title: Gradle dependencies
docs.text:
Add the Peekniko storage adapter for debug builds and the no-op client for release builds. Use the same Peekniko version for both artifacts:

build.gradle.kts
dependencies {
    debugImplementation("io.github.otacon.peekniko:storage-sqldelight:<peekniko-version>")
    releaseImplementation("io.github.otacon.peekniko:client-noop:<peekniko-version>")
}

If your app already uses SQLDelight, no additional SQLDelight dependencies are needed. Otherwise, add the runtime, coroutine extensions, and Android driver to debug builds, using the same SQLDelight version for all three:

build.gradle.kts
dependencies {
    debugImplementation("app.cash.sqldelight:runtime:<sqldelight-version>")
    debugImplementation("app.cash.sqldelight:coroutines-extensions:<sqldelight-version>")
    debugImplementation("app.cash.sqldelight:android-driver:<sqldelight-version>")
}

docs.title: Configure Peekniko and storage
docs.text:
Add storage to your startup configuration before creating your HTTP client.

import peekniko.Peekniko
import peekniko.storage.sqldelight.sqlDelightStorage

Peekniko.configure {
    sqlDelightStorage(name = "peekniko.db")
}

Peekniko saves the database in your app's database directory using the name you provide.

docs.title: Open Peekniko
docs.text:
Peekniko's inspector is built with Compose Multiplatform, so your app needs the Compose Desktop runtime for its OS on the classpath. Compose Desktop apps already have it; other JVM apps can add it with the Compose Gradle plugin:

build.gradle.kts
dependencies {
    implementation(compose.desktop.currentOs)
}

Open the inspector in its own window:

import peekniko.Peekniko
import peekniko.open

Peekniko.open()

Or embed it in a Compose window you manage yourself:

import peekniko.Peekniko
import peekniko.ui.Screen

Window(onCloseRequest = { showPeekniko = false }, title = "Peekniko") {
    Peekniko.Screen(onClose = { showPeekniko = false })
}

Peekniko also adds a system tray icon that shows new calls and opens the inspector.

import peekniko.ktor.plugin
import io.ktor.client.HttpClient
import io.ktor.client.engine.okhttp.OkHttp

val client = HttpClient(OkHttp) {
    install(Peekniko.plugin)
}

Use the regular adapter for builds where you want to capture traffic, and the no-op adapter for builds where you don't.

docs.title: SQLDelight storage
docs.text: Keep your captured requests and responses between app launches with SQLDelight storage.

docs.title: Gradle dependencies
docs.text:
Add the Peekniko core and storage adapter, plus SQLDelight's:

  • runtime
  • coroutine extensions
  • SQLite driver

Use the same Peekniko version for both artifacts and the same SQLDelight version for all SQLDelight artifacts:

build.gradle.kts
dependencies {
    // Debug builds
    implementation("io.github.otacon.peekniko:client-core:<peekniko-version>")
    implementation("io.github.otacon.peekniko:storage-sqldelight:<peekniko-version>")
    implementation("app.cash.sqldelight:runtime:<sqldelight-version>")
    implementation("app.cash.sqldelight:coroutines-extensions:<sqldelight-version>")
    implementation("app.cash.sqldelight:sqlite-driver:<sqldelight-version>")
}

docs.title: Configure Peekniko and storage
docs.text:
Add storage to your startup configuration before creating your HTTP client:

import peekniko.Peekniko
import peekniko.storage.sqldelight.sqlDelightStorage

Peekniko.configure {
    sqlDelightStorage(name = "peekniko.db")
}

Use a filename or path for the database. Peekniko creates it for you if it doesn't exist yet.

docs.title: Swift Package Manager
docs.text:
In a Swift-only app, add https://github.com/Otacon/peekniko as a package dependency and pick a release version. The package has two products, both used with import PeeknikoCore:

Product Contents Link it into PeeknikoKit The inspector, URLSession capture, and SQLDelight storage Debug or internal app targets PeeknikoKitNoop The same API, doing nothing Production app targets

Link only one of the two into an app target. Swift Package Manager can't switch products by build configuration, so use a separate app target (or scheme) for debug builds. PeeknikoKit links SQLite for you.

In a Kotlin Multiplatform app, add the Gradle dependencies from each page instead.

docs.title: Configure Peekniko
docs.text:
Configure Peekniko once when your app starts, before creating your HTTP client:

import peekniko.Peekniko

Peekniko.configure {

}

By default, Peekniko keeps captures in memory. To keep them between app launches, add SQLDelight storage.

From Swift:

Peekniko.shared.configure { configuration in
    configuration.inMemoryStorage(maxApiCalls: 100)
}

docs.title: Open Peekniko
docs.text:
The inspector is a Compose Multiplatform screen. Present it from the main thread:

import peekniko.Peekniko
import peekniko.open

Peekniko.open()

From Swift, with the framework exporting Peekniko:

Peekniko.shared.open(from: nil)

To embed it in your own Compose UI, use Peekniko.Screen().

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
Peekniko posts a quiet notification listing the latest calls once notifications are authorized. It asks for permission the first time its screen opens, unless your app has already asked.

If your app sets its own UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate, forward to Peekniko:

func userNotificationCenter(_ center: UNUserNotificationCenter, willPresent notification: UNNotification) async -> UNNotificationPresentationOptions {
    Peekniko.shared.isPeeknikoNotification(notification: notification) ? [.list] : []
}

func userNotificationCenter(_ center: UNUserNotificationCenter, didReceive response: UNNotificationResponse) async {
    _ = Peekniko.shared.handleNotificationResponse(response: response)
}

Without a delegate of your own, no setup is needed.

In a Swift-only app, SQLDelight storage is already part of the PeeknikoKit product from Swift Package Manager, which also links SQLite. Skip to Configure Peekniko and storage.

docs.title: URLSession
docs.text: Capture URLSession traffic by registering Peekniko's URLProtocol.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
In a Kotlin Multiplatform app, add the dependency to your shared module and export it from your framework:

build.gradle.kts
kotlin {
    sourceSets {
        iosMain.dependencies {
            api("io.github.otacon.peekniko:client-core:<peekniko-version>")
        }
    }
}

In a Swift-only app, add the PeeknikoKit product with Swift Package Manager, then import PeeknikoCore.

To try local changes, build the framework and add the library-ios folder to Xcode as a local package:

./gradlew :library-ios:assemblePeeknikoCoreDebugXCFramework

docs.title: Register the protocol
docs.text:
Register the protocol once at startup, after configuring Peekniko and before creating requests:

Peekniko.shared.registerUrlProtocol()

Sessions created with their own URLSessionConfiguration need the protocol added explicitly:

let configuration = URLSessionConfiguration.default
Peekniko.shared.addUrlProtocol(configuration: configuration)

From Kotlin, the same functions are Peekniko.registerUrlProtocol() and Peekniko.addUrlProtocol(configuration).
